title: Prefill demultiplexer and proactive kernel sampler to reduce tail latency in continuous batching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Reduce p95/p99 tail latency for continuous batching workloads by splitting incoming prefill traffic into lightweight cost classes and proactively sampling kernel runtimes to inform per-class admission policies.

Background: Current continuous batching treats most requests homogeneously which causes long-tailed service times when a few large/odd-shaped sequences hit expensive kernel paths or cause KV cache hotspots. Previous work improved admission heuristics, but we still observe p99 regressions during mixed workloads and microbursts. This ticket implements a lightweight demultiplexer that classifies requests at admission time and a proactive kernel sampler that maintains low-overhead runtime estimates for each class (seq-len ranges, attention mode, quantization variant).

Approach:
- Add a prefill demultiplexer layer that tags requests into cost classes (tiny/short/medium/long/kv-hot) using a fast heuristic (token-length, requested decode length, presence of long-context flags, detector for KV-heavy templates).
- Maintain per-class soft-queues with separate admission budgets and a shared reclaim pool to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Implement a proactive kernel sampler that periodically runs short latency probes across representative model variants (float16, int8/4 quant, fused attention vs unfused) at controlled tokens to update a small online table of expected kernel costs. Sampler runs at low priority and adapts probe frequency based on variance in recent estimates.
- Use sampler outputs to compute per-class kernel-affinity scores. Admission uses a combined score: estimated kernel cost + current queue delay + slot availability to decide whether to admit immediately, delay (soft backoff), or route to a cheaper model variant.
- KV hotspot mitigation: detect repeated attention to same KV keys and temporarily isolate those flows into a dedicated class with capped reservations to avoid cache eviction storms.
- Instrumentation: expose per-class p50/p95/p99, admission reject rates, sampler variance, and kernel-affinity histograms to the runtime dashboard.

Non-goals: full rework of kernel selection logic (this is advisory input for existing kernel planner) and large model recompilation. This ticket focuses on admission & sampling layer and light integration with kernel planner outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-class admission implemented and configurable via runtime config toggles (enabled=false by default)
Proactive kernel sampler publishes per-class mean and variance and updates at configurable intervals
End-to-end e2e benchmark shows >=15% reduction in p99 for mixed short+long workload compared to baseline on internal perf cluster
No measurable throughput regression (>2%) for steady-state homogeneous short-sequence workload
Dashboard exposes new metrics and a heatmap for kernel-affinity vs sequence-length
Automated unit + integration tests for demultiplexer logic, sampler correctness, and a stress test for KV-hotspot isolation
updates: 2026-02-25 - Created ticket. Draft design sketched in confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Prefill+Demultiplexer+Design
2026-02-28 - Spike complete: implemented local prototype of class heuristics and measured classifier overhead ~0.8us/request on test harness. Notes: heuristics need to be robust to templated prompts.
2026-03-03 - Decided to keep classes coarse (5 bins) to limit scheduler state. Trade-off: fewer classes simplifies admission but may hide outliers. Documented trade-off in design doc.

2026-03-05 - Integrated a minimal kernel sampler using existing microbench harness. Sampling cost observed ~0.2% GPU cycles when run at 1 probe/sec across N=4 variants. Initial sampler code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128

2026-03-08 - Run against internal mixed workload (short+long+kv-heavy). Preliminary results: p99 down 18% on a 4-GPU shard but p95 improvement only 7%. Observed a regression in slot utilization during peaks; mitigations proposed in next update.

2026-03-10 - Proposal: add shared reclaim pool and soft-defer window of 25ms per class to smooth bursts. Preparing PR and will run larger scale perf cluster tests next week. Assigned Marco for coordinator tasks.

Pending - Need design review from kernel planner team (cc: Elena Park) and SRE sign-off for sampler scheduling policy. Linking runtime SLO dashboard: https://dashboards.internal.redwood.com/d/runtime/prefill-demux
